done.why: I saw a few places and got a gift from the sailor. Nothing pulled me toward a clear goal, so I stopped early.

about: An underground cave world. A dream-wizard says to seek him when worthy. I wandered caves, a cliff and a shore, picking up a lantern, bread and a vial.

moments.note: Moving south into the dark warned of a grue. I had to guess to turn on the lantern.
Pulling the sword got a joke: Who do you think you are? Arthur?
I could not climb back up the rope and the chest was locked. I felt trapped.
I didn't know how to get down from the ledge. 'scramble down' was not understood, 'go down' worked.
Saying hello to the sailor freed him and he gave me a gift. I would not have known to say it without the hint in his description.

wished: To know what the vial is for
To get the locked chest open
A hint about how to speak to the sailor, since talking to him in a sentence failed

lines.line: I have waited three ages for someone to say those words and save me from sailing this endless ocean.
lines.why: A charming payoff for a puzzle solved by listening to the description.

lines.line: Who do you think you are? Arthur?

fun.why: Some charming moments, but I stopped early and no goal emerged.

engagement.why: The sailor puzzle drew me in. The one-way descent cut my options.

difficulty.why: Mostly gentle, but the parser was picky and the one-way drop was a surprise.

interestingness.why: Varied locations and playful details like the cliff, the ocean and the sailor.

prose.why: Evocative room descriptions, such as the sunlit oasis cliff.
